title: The bag that copies
notes: Keep one adult at each table and reset every fresh story to the same two original counters. First routes: K-1 P1-2; grades 2-3 P1-2; grades 4-5 P1, then P2-3. Before the first chance question (grades 2-3 P2, grades 4-5 P1), pairs draw without looking for about ten two-draw copying games, then about ten return-only games, and pool the final bags on a class chart: a conjecture for the counting to test. The games take about 15 minutes. A chart of 20 pooled games of each kind shows fewer two-red, two-blue bags for copying than for returning only about four times in five, so a chart that does not is ordinary chance; the exact count decides. On return, K-1 can find four-draw stories or work backward one step (P3-4). Grades 2-3 can compare return-only sampling and reordered words (P3-4), then larger final bags (P5-6). Grades 4-5 can make the 24-history argument (P4), the four-draw count (P5), or pursue the arbitrary-length conjecture (P6). Keep exact history counts distinct from trial frequencies.
